item.title: Soot spikes from traffic and holiday bonfires emerge in Addis Ababa air record
item.description: An air pollution monitoring network has provided one of the most detailed long-term views yet of the role of black carbon, or soot produced by fires, diesel vehicles and other combustion sources, in Ethiopia's capital, Addis Ababa. The detailed measurements show how pollution changes by time of day and season, including increases associated with rush-hour traffic and holiday celebrations. The findings are relevant to cities around the world, including in the United States. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient Egyptian tomb shows how burial trends changed over hundreds of years
item.description: The Theban Necropolis, opposite Luxor, consists of more than 400 tombs. In a new Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology study, researchers in Spain examined part of one of these tombs—chamber three in tomb TT 209—to reconstruct how this burial space was used and reused between its construction during the Twenty-fifth Dynasty (754–656 BCE) and the Ptolemaic period (305–30 BCE), when it was abandoned. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 3,000-year-old inscription naming Masn may help archaeologists identify the lost Egyptian city
item.description: A remarkable sandstone lintel inscribed with the titles of Ramesses II was uncovered at Tell Abu Seify. This inscription reveals valuable information about the restoration of a statue of Horus, the Lord of Masn. Such findings bolster the theory that this site may very well be the fabled lost city of Masn, showcasing evolution from a significant religious and military hub to an industrial quarry through recent excavations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

Mohamed Youssouf Bathily was convicted by the Bamaka court of criminal conspiracy and discrediting the state alongside Rokia Doumbia, a noted campaigner. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: La epidemia de ébola se propaga a una velocidad nunca antes vista en RD Congo: "Mata una persona cada 30 minutos"
item.description: El brote se convirtió en el más mortífero en la historia del país este lunes, cuando la cifra de víctimas ascendió a 2.325. Muchos pacientes mueren antes de llegar a los centros médicos y en Bunia, epicentro de la crisis, casi no hay medidas de prevención. Piden un alto el fuego humanitario para que los médicos puedan llegar hasta los enfermos. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.
item.dc:creator: Clarin.com - Home

item.title: Hichilema takes early lead as Zambia election count passes halfway
item.description: President Hakainde Hichilema has taken an early lead in Zambia’s presidential election, securing nearly 59 percent of votes counted in 135 of 226 constituencies. The result puts him on course for a second-term victory, though the final tally is still underway. Fuente: Africanews.
item.dc:creator: editorial@africanews.com (Dominic Wabwireh)

item.title: Ebola outbreak becomes deadliest in DR Congo’s history
item.description: The Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is now the deadliest the country has ever faced, the UN’s World Health Organization (WHO) said on Monday. Publicado también por: The Jerusalem Post - International. Fuente: UN News.

item.title: Senegal’s historic pirogue regatta brings Saint-Louis to life
item.description: Thousands gathered in Saint-Louis on Saturday for the city’s traditional pirogue regatta, a centuries-old competition rooted in the fishing community of Guet-Ndar. Beyond the fierce rivalry on the water, the event celebrates heritage, solidarity and a legacy passed down through generations. Fuente: Africanews.

item.title: Somalia troops and armed opposition clash in heavy Baidoa fighting as civilian toll rises
item.description: Fresh fighting in the city could compound a dire humanitarian crisis in the area. Baidoa hosts hundreds of thousands of displaced people; one in four children at refugee sites is malnourished. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.

item.title: Cholera outbreak spreads in Cameroon as cases top 1,000
item.description: A cholera outbreak is spreading across northern Cameroon, with more than 1,000 cases and 28 deaths reported since mid-July, according to health authorities. Fuente: Africanews.

item.title: Cameroon wins first Women's Africa Cup of Nations title
item.description: Cameroon defeated tournament newcomers Malawi 3-0 in the final to win its first Women's Africa Cup of Nations title. Marie Ngah Manga scored twice and Naomi Eto added another goal. Both finalists, along with Morocco and Algeria, qualified for next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. Publicado también por: Al Jazeera English, Africanews. Fuente: France 24 - English.
